images.seen: Near East, Egypt, Kerma and Indus all in plausible places; compiled adds the Mari, Yamhad, Qatna, Eshnunna, Larsa and Isin states Cliopatria lacks; the Qatna Palmyra disc is a separate exclave by dossier design; nothing outside its region.

WRONG: First Sealand dynasty drawn as an 8 x 5.3 degree rectangle (42-50 E, 27-32.3 N) over the Saudi desert, Kuwait and the Gulf coast, 1,477 cells; Cliopatria's marsh shape is a small patch at the Gulf head. Patched.

Hammurabi's Babylonia (Euphrates to Mari, Eshnunna, the lower plain) matches the dossier's adjust; two small Babylonian specks stand next to Elam in the Zagros foothills (the 128-cell Elam/Babylonia ordering artefact), harmless.
25 states, no stray cells or speckle; only the Sealand rectangle stood out (fixed in the stage).

Egypt and Kerma: Kerma holds a thin Nile strip of Lower Nubia interleaved with Egyptian cells from -1750 (ledger gain from the Middle Kingdom, page silent on the date); odd looking but the pages cannot improve it.
Isin (small), Larsa (large, to the Eshnunna border), Babylonia (small) match the Rim-Sin I dossiers; no fault.
Sealand now a compact shape: marsh core, Dhi-Qar and Basra, Uruk; Saudi desert and Gulf gone.
Nippur and Isin joined to the Sealand as one connected body that now abuts Babylonia, as the Samsu-iluna page's year-29 evidence has it.

issues.what: First Sealand dynasty drawn as the box 42-50 E, 27-32.3 N (Saudi desert, Kuwait, Gulf): the keyframe -1732 correction and the found event share that polygon; 1,477 cells at the end of -1732, 1,320 of them nobody's.

Nippur and Isin: the old box gave them to the Sealand from -1732; the pages put the loss of Nippur and Isin late in Samsu-iluna's reign (records stop in year 29, Nippur recognises Ilum-ma-ili by his death).

The same box polygon is in first-sealand-dynasty keyframes -1700, -1600, -1500 and in the found event (ledger/0). A patch cannot change a found event, so the draft now logs a keyframe snap at -1732 (removes 1,320 cells the founding event gave); harmless to the map.
elam / first-sealand-dynasty conflict (Khuzestan, 122 cell-years after the patch, 244 before): Elam is smaller and wins; the pages give no border for the marsh.

Indus Valley snap of 1,638 cells at -1800: the draft of m1900-m1801 already re-adds the Mature shape at -1900 because the -2000 keyframe (no `to`, so alive to -1801) is unioned with the -1900 correction; my window's -1800 keyframe snaps it back to the 1,389-cell Late Harappan shape. The anchor at m1800 therefore holds 3,027 cells for -1900..-1801.

Elam / Babylonia at -1760 (128 cell-years): Babylonia's keyframe claims Ilam, Khuzestan and Kermanshah foothill cells, Elam wins by size, then Elam's own -1760 keyframe drops them, so they are nobody's until Babylonia's -1750 keyframe takes them. No page opened gives that border.

Kerma takes a Nile strip of Lower Nubia from the Middle Kingdom in -1750, drawn as a ragged strip interleaved with Egyptian desert cells; the Kerma page says only that Classic Kerma (1750-1500) controlled the 1st to 4th Cataracts and that Egyptian control weakened in the 13th Dynasty and Second Intermediate Period, with no date for the takeover.
Middle Kingdom of Egypt gains 970 desert cells (Western and Eastern Desert, Cliopatria shape) at -1800 on a confidence-1 event; the dossier itself says the page is silent.
Qatna drawn as two discs (Homs and Palmyra, 'its easternmost city'); Palmyra is an exclave.

Other packet flags (eshnunna/assyria 38, eshnunna/mari 32, mari/yamhad 19, babylonia/assyria 38 cell-years; snaps of 19 to 296 cells for eshnunna, yamhad, mari, assyria, kerma, larsa, isin) each rest on a ledger event the dossier itself dates; the smaller state winning is right in each. The hierarchy row assyria of babylonia (-1751..-1712) matches Babylonia ledger/6 and /8.

dossier_requests.what: Replace the polygon [[42,27],[50,27],[50,32.3],[42,32.3]] in ledger/0 (found) and in keyframes first-sealand-dynasty_-1732, _-1700, _-1600 and _-1500 by the Cliopatria marsh shape plus Dhi-Qar, Al-Basrah and place Uruk 60 km (about 157 cells); add Nippur and Isin (place 40 km each, 27 cells) from -1721.
dossier_requests.why: The box covers the Saudi desert, Kuwait and the Gulf (1,320 cells outside any Sumerian land); the page has Sealand pottery 'at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that' and Nippur and Isin leaving Babylonia in Samsu-iluna's year 29.

dossier_requests.what: Give keyframe indus-valley-civilization_-2000 an explicit `to` of -1901.
dossier_requests.why: Without it the keyframe stays alive to Cliopatria's row end (-1801) and, unioned with the -1900 keyframe, keeps the Mature 3,027-cell shape for -1900..-1801; its own note says it holds only -2000..-1901.

problems: cross-window: first-sealand-dynasty keyframes -1700, -1600 and -1500 (windows m1700-m1601 and later) carry the same Saudi-desert box; I did not override them (outside my years), so from -1700 the box returns at the next window's first snap until a dossier fix or an override by that window's agent (keyframe_overrides of first-sealand-dynasty_-1700 in m1700-m1601, the others in their windows).
